subject: Time-to-first-token handshake: mode preference, capacity snapshot, and next steps
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira@fastledger.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: procure@fastledger.com
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2027 15:20:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo recap — TTFT targets and streaming mode preference

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Quick recap while it's fresh and to capture agreed next steps. Key points we covered: 

- FastLedger goal: user-visible response for the mobile app to feel instantaneous on chat features. Product team suggested a target of ~150–200ms perceived latency for the first visible token in the UI (iOS/Android median).
- Mobile constraint: unreliable long-lived websockets on older devices; some customers will prefer SSE polling-style fallbacks. Samira said ~30% of current active users are on carriers with flaky websocket behavior.
- Throughput & concurrency: estimate for initial pilot is 600 concurrent active users at peak, with occasional microbursts up to ~2k concurrent sessions during market open.
- Data policy: FastLedger requires that inference logs related to PII be avoided; we'll route telemetry to a separate telemetry-only retention with redact-by-default.

Immediate asks I noted: 
1) Redwood to propose a TTFT SLO candidate (p50/p95/p99) and recommended streaming mode (WS primary vs SSE primary) with fallback policy.
2) Redwood infra to share a capacity snapshot that maps the pilot 600c sustained / 2k burst to Dedicated pool sizing and expected cost envelope.
3) FastLedger to send their security questionnaire (we received it — thanks) and procurement contact to begin contract timelines.

Ben / Marcus: can you weigh in on recommended SLOs and a short pilot config we can present to them? I attached the questionnaire and a draft pilot-capacity workbook.

Best,
Logan Wright
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Cell: (415) 555-0123

Attachments: FastLedger_Security_Questionnaire.pdf (PDF), pilot-capacity-snapshot.xlsx (Excel)

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap — TTFT targets and streaming mode preference

Thanks Logan — helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The product team is comfortable with a 180ms p95 TTFT target for the pilot as long as p50 is <80ms on average. The UX team will measure perceived latency with a small instrumented cohort.
- WebSocket preference: we prefer WebSocket as primary in web clients, but for mobile we'd like SSE as the primary mode with automatic upgrade to WebSocket where stable. Important: low memory footprint on iOS must be preserved.
- Concurrency refinement: 600 concurrent active users is our conservative launch estimate. Bursts historically have lasted up to 20–90 seconds, so burst-handling rules matter more than sustained headroom.
- Procurement: please send standard SOW + pilot terms. procurement@fastledger.com will own contract pathing.

Will review the capacity workbook and loop in infra early if I have questions.

— Samira
Head of Product, FastLedger
samira@fastledger.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Samira Khan <samira@fastledger.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2027 09:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap — TTFT targets and streaming mode preference

Appended some technical recommendations and the pilot config we'd propose based on their numbers. High level: reachable, but requires tuned batching + prefix caching and a small warm pool.

Recommendation summary:
- TTFT SLO: target 180ms p95; aspirational 120ms p50. We'll size for 180ms p95 with fallback to a lighter-quantized model if queueing exceeds a short threshold.
- Streaming mode: support hybrid policy: Mobile clients - SSE primary, WebSocket upgrade when negotiation indicates carrier stability. Web clients - WebSocket primary with SSE fallback. We'll use a short handshake (HTTP/1.1 SSE) with user-agent-based heuristics.
- Chunk cadence: default chunk windows of 120–200ms depending on payload size. For short chat messages we recommend 120–150ms to keep perceived typing fluid; for long generative responses use 200–300ms to maximize throughput efficiency.
- Concurrency/capacity: Pilot config (estimate): 
  - Sustained headroom: 600 concurrent active sessions => map to 8 GPU instances (A100-type equivalence) with continuous batching enabled.
  - Burst headroom: support 2k concurrent for short bursts by enabling autoscale policy (3x burst capacity, warm fraction of 25%).
  - KV/prefix caching: keep a 2-minute warm cache for active sessions where possible to reduce token-gen latency on repeated prompts.
- Fallbacks: auto-failover to a quantized model variant when per-request queue > 75ms; route to region fallback if localized capacity is saturated.

Pilot acceptance criteria (suggested):
1) Measured TTFT p95 <= 180ms for instrumented cohort (n=5000 calls per day) for 3 consecutive business days.
2) No more than 1% of sessions experiencing disconnects from streaming handshake in mobile cohort.
3) CPU and memory per mobile client under threshold X (we'll provide specific footprint after SDK tests).

I'll attach a short Excel with instance mapping and cost band estimate. Logan — happy to join the next call with FastLedger infra to walk through the autoscale knobs.

Ben Carter
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
